# known-unresolved-refs.txt — the T-73b reference-resolution ratchet
# (issue #563, AC-6.6, .codearbiter/specs/release-portable-fixture.md,
# .codearbiter/plans/portable-release-and-protected-state.md).
#
# Every path reference extracted from the INSTALLED release SKILL.md
# (plugins/ca/skills/release/SKILL.md, materialized via `git archive HEAD`)
# that does NOT resolve against the scratch plugin root or the scratch
# consumer repo, per `.github/scripts/test_consumer_smoke.py`'s
# ReferenceResolutionRatchetTest.
#
# This is a RATCHET, not a red test: `test_reference_resolution_ratchet`
# asserts the computed set equals this file EXACTLY, in either direction. A
# shrink not recorded here fails just as loudly as a new contaminating
# reference appearing. Every entry below is a hardcoded, this-repo-specific
# reference the release skill carries because the skill rewrite (T-41a-d,
# A-6.0) has not yet run:
#
#   - the Targets table (`| ca | v | plugins/ca/.claude-plugin/plugin.json |
#     ... |`) hardcodes every plugin's manifest/changelog/artifact paths as
#     literal prose; T-41a replaces the table with `load_targets()` and none
#     of these literals survive as text;
#   - every `python3 .github/scripts/_releaselib.py ...` / `tools/build-
#     host-packages.py` invocation assumes the skill executes with THIS
#     repo as its working tree; T-41b repoints every such helper call under
#     `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}`;
#   - `.github/published-tags.json` is hardcoded in Phase 3 step 5; T-41c
#     reads it from the row's `provenance-manifest` field instead.
#
# Entries are removed here in the SAME commit that removes the
# corresponding reference from the skill — never in a separate cleanup
# commit, and never by widening the extractor to stop seeing them. T-79
# asserts this file is empty and retires the ratchet.
#
# MEDIUM-4 (adversarial review 2026-07-31), ruling: `check_badge_
# consistency.py`, `check_tag_immutability.py`, `payload_scope.py`, and
# `test_release_lib.py` below are named in PROSE ("CI's badge-consistency
# guard (...)", "pinned by ...") rather than executed by the skill itself —
# under the spec's own measurement rule they are not contaminating on
# their own terms, so T-41a-d's "no .github/scripts/ invocation remains"
# criterion will not touch them and T-79 would otherwise be unreachable.
# Ruling is to keep ONE list (a blocking/non-blocking split would create a
# parking space where a real invocation could hide, AC-6.3 precedent:
# `decision-lifecycle` was reworded, not carved out) and extend T-41b's
# scope to reword these four mentions too, the same way. This comment is
# the marker naming T-41b as the task that clears all four; do not remove
# these lines except in the commit that does the reword.
#
# MEDIUM-3 (adversarial review 2026-07-31): the three payloads below marked
# "glob" are new in this remediation (HIGH-1 — the extractor previously
# could not see an executed glob at all); the release-skill payloads under
# `ca-codex`/`ca-pi` (`routines/release/SKILL.md`, an identical copy of
# this same contamination) contribute NO entry not already listed here —
# verified by `ReferenceResolutionRatchetTest` scanning all five installed
# copies and asserting the UNIONED unresolved set against this file.
